page: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for workloads requiring dedicated graphics processing and balanced compute resources. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 56.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB per core. For acceleration, the server is equipped with two NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs from the Turing family, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance and highly efficient small-to-medium language model inference capabilities. The instance achieved a strong Passmark memory score of 2838.84, although large block memory write bandwidth was weaker at 19.55 GB/sec. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the server reached top-tier performance with 9506.12 tokens per second for prompt processing and 387.2 tokens per second for text generation. Similarly, with a medium 7B model, it maintained top-tier speeds of 1841.54 tokens per second for prompt processing and 67.32 tokens per second for text generation. General CPU benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and multi-core, fall within the average range.

Given its dual-GPU architecture and dedicated CPU cores, the rtx5000-56 offers a specialized hardware profile for parallel processing tasks. It is highly suited for small-to-medium large language model inference, ray tracing, and image processing. The inclusion of dedicated physical cores and local SSD storage makes it a viable option for workloads requiring predictable compute performance without hyperthreading overhead. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server provides a dense allocation of GPU memory and dedicated processing power, making it suitable for development and deployment of machine learning models and graphics rendering pipelines that do not require the highest-tier enterprise data center GPUs.
